4.text: “Soft men,” of course, are supposed to excel in all branches of shamanism,

5.text: including the ventriloquistic art, notwithstanding the fact that they are supposed

6.text: to be women. Because of their supernatural protectors, they are dreaded

7.text: even by untransformed shamans, who avoid having any contests with them,

8.text: especially with the younger ones, because they are exceedingly “bashful,” and

9.text: readily stand back before the pretensions of other people; but afterward the

10.text: supernatural husband retaliates for the slight.

11.text: Of all transformed shamans whom I have chanced to know, the most

12.text: remarkable was Tiluˊwg̣i (Plate XXXIII, Fig. 1), of whom I spoke in an

13.text: earlier part of this chapter. I met him at a small trade-gathering among

14.text: the camps of Reindeer people on the Wolverene River. He, together with

15.text: a party of traders, came from the Chukchee Peninsula. He was of Maritime

16.text: origin; but his family had some reindeer, and spent most of their time tending

17.text: the herd. Tiluˊwg̣i was young, and looked about thirty-five years of age.

20.text: I staid for two days in his tent, and slept in his small inner room,

21.text: which was hardly large enough to accommodate four sleepers. Thus I had

22.text: a chance to observe quite closely the details of his physique, which, of course,

23.text: were all masculine. He refused obstinately, however, to permit himself to be

24.text: fully inspected. His husband, Yaˊtirg̣ɪn, tempted by the offered price, tried

25.text: to persuade him, but, after some useless attempts, was at last silenced by one

26.text: scowling look from his peculiar “wife.” He felt sorry, however, that I had

27.text: been baffled in gratifying my curiosity, and therefore offered me, to use his

28.text: own words, his eyes in place of my own.

29.text: He described the physique of Tiluˊwg̣i as wholly masculine, and well

30.text: developed besides. He confessed that he was sorry for it, but he hoped

31.text: that in time, with the aid of his keˊlet, Tiluˊwg̣i would be able to equal the

32.text: real “soft men” of old, and to change the organs of his sex altogether, which

33.text: would be much more convenient than the present state. Notwithstanding all

34.text: this, and even the brownish down which covered his upper lip, Tiluˊwg̣i’s

35.text: face, encircled with braids of thick hair arranged after the manner of Chukchee

36.text: women, looked very different from masculine faces. It was something like a

37.text: female tragic mask fitted to a body of a giantess of a race different from

38.text: our own. All the ways of this strange creature were decidedly feminine.
